brief: The Nasdaq has fallen 7% in five trading days, erasing its 2026 gains, as a broader equity reversal (the world's largest company down 43% in five weeks) spreads into gold and copper. Wilson ties this to a deteriorating liquidity backdrop: the dollar is retesting highs last seen after the 2024 election on hawkish Fed commentary, and broad financial conditions have tightened rapidly enough to bite markets. His rule of thumb: a 100bp financial-conditions tightening this fast costs about 50bp of growth over 12 months. Comparable 100-150bp tightenings produced 10-20% S&P 500 drawdowns in 2018, 2023 and 2025, with the current move at the low end of that band, though energy prices and AI capex look to have turned. Separately, Nvidia's customer and supply-chain financing commitments grew from $366bn to $518bn this quarter, deepening doubts about capex sustainability after Jensen's removal. Hedge funds have sharply cut AI-capex-winner positioning and Goldman's Prime book long/short ratio hit a 15-year low. Wilson forecasts 18% S&P 500 EPS growth for 2027 but sees the market in the late stage of a liquidity-driven unwind that could still reach a 20% pullback, and now favors long bonds paired with long equities over this year's short-bonds hedge.
